source.original_title: 05/22/2026 - Parth Shukla x Harry Edmonds KFS
source.display_title: 05/22/2026 - Parth Shukla x Harry Edmonds KFS  — Closed

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Setter code taken from the title suffix. The recording begins mid-frame at 00:00:00 and no setter is named anywhere in the recorded portion, so there is no in-call corroboration.

prospect.name: Parth Shukla
prospect.location: Canada, Eastern time zone; moving to another city the week of the call (keys on the 28th)
prospect.occupation: Software engineer — desk-bound, "most of the time, it's just sitting with a computer"
prospect.family_status: Married; wife is following the same diet and shares the fitness goal
prospect.training_background: Down from 98 kg to 88-90 kg over a few months, almost entirely through diet change. Weekend lane swimming, roughly 45 minutes of free swim, though not consistently. Bought a single kettlebell after watching Trevor's reels and does basic work with it on and off. Follows Trevor's free stretching content almost daily. No fixed routine and never had a coach.

signals: Self-started and already executing — lost 10 kg on his own, cut sugar, processed food and most wheat, and brought his wife with him
Competitive framing rather than rescue framing: "I want to be the fittest in my group... my bros, my friends, they're all, like, you know, have gotten lazy"

Weaker fit than the label implies: at 5'11" and 90 kg targeting 80 kg with "stubborn belly fat" to lose, he is mid-transformation rather than polishing a finished physique, and he is 29 — below the 30-plus floor he himself believed the programme had

goals.text: Lose the stubborn belly fat and get to around 80 kg
Build defined muscle in arms and legs without becoming bulky
Feel confident with his shirt off or in a tank top in summer
Be the fittest in his friendship group by his early-to-mid thirties
Have a definite structure he knows will work rather than piecing workouts together online
Be the example that gets his wife and friends back in shape

pains.text: No structure — "maybe it's just a lack of structure, which is just like you get boosted when you look at some, maybe like some workouts here and there, and then you try to follow by yourself"
Grinds at self-directed programmes for months, sees no results and quits
Desk-bound work with no physical engagement — "the only thing you're engaging is your fingers and your brain"
Uncertain whether he is doing the movements correctly or whether they suit him
Morning training happens only when he manages to get up early; otherwise it slips
Swimming twice a week has stopped moving the needle on its own

objections.raw_quote: I mean, so honestly, like, I'm moving this week, so I would probably start something like this in the first week... Given, like, this week I have to move to the other city and, you know, drive everything on a truck and take things there. But, like, something from the first week of June, yes, I'm definitely willing to start.
objections.rep_response: Removed the conflict rather than pushing through it — booked onboarding before the move and explained that the six-month clock starts on the first workout day, so no time is lost: "your first day of the six months or the 12 months would be your first workout day, no you don't lose any time."

offer.payment_plan_terms: Two payments of CAD 4,140, the second due before the halfway point of the programme: "either 8,280 Canadian upfront, or if you do it in two payments, it's 4,140" and "we'll just do the 50% now and then we will do the other 50% as long as it is done before halfway through." A monthly option was mentioned and steered away from: "you can do it monthly, but it works out to be in 10,000 Canadian pretty much for the six months." Prospect chose two payments on a credit card.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: "all the results are guaranteed. So the way we do that, and the only way we can guarantee results for everybody is based on the weight of the kettlebell that you use. So our guarantee is that at the start of the training, let's say you're using a 25 pound kettlebell or a 30 pound kettlebell, by the end of the six months, you're going to be swinging around a 20 pound heavier kettlebell for the same intensity and the same reps and the same volume."

evidence: Chose the six-month tier and the two-payment structure: "I would probably do two payments"
Confirmed the payment instrument — rep: "Did you want to do it on like a Visa, MasterCard, credit card?" — prospect: "Yeah, the credit card should be okay"
Trevor onboarding call booked live for Tuesday 26th at 1:15pm Eastern, checked against his work calendar
Explicit commitment when asked: "You ready to rock and roll?" — "Oh, yeah."

Counter-evidence: the recording is stopped by the rep at the moment payment details are taken — "I want to make sure I get all your information correct. Let me just remove the recording" — so the transaction is not evidenced as completed on the recording, only as commenced
Counter-evidence: no agreement email, signature, welcome email or Skool link was mentioned at any point
outcome.next_step: First payment of CAD 4,140 taken on the call by credit card with the balance due before the halfway point; onboarding call with Trevor on Tuesday 26th at 1:15pm Eastern before the house move; kettlebells (25-35 lb) and a door pull-up bar to be bought before the first workout in the first week of June

notable.note: A clean close and the best-run call in the batch on commitment sequencing — time commitment and start timing were both secured before the price. Three things for a principal. First, the prospect stated on the record that he believed the coaching had a 30-plus age floor and that he is not yet 30; the rep never addressed it and sold him anyway. Second, the whole transaction was denominated in Canadian dollars and the number moved during the call from 8,200 to 8,280, with the monthly alternative quoted at roughly 10,000 CAD. Third, the rep stopped the recording to take card details, which is sound practice for card data but means the corpus has no evidence of payment completion. Also worth noting: the prospect is vegetarian and the nutrition pillar is built on red meat, eggs and dairy; his direct question about that was answered in one line.

quality.notes: Recording begins mid-sentence during the rep's frame, so an unknown amount of P1 precedes the file. Swapping is frequent and sometimes mid-turn — the rep's line "Cool. I know you said you want to get in the best shape of your life" at 00:03:40 sits under the prospect label, as do parts of the pricing exchange, and several prospect replies sit under Harry Edmonds. Two long passages around 00:07:00 and 00:29:00 run the two speakers together in a single block with no turn breaks.
